Name: Mod Template Builder - With instruction on how to make your first mod
Author: ZeroXPatch
Description:
[center][color=#ffff00][size=6]Mod Starter Kit - Mod Template Builder[/size][/color][/center]
Starting a Stardew Valley mod can feel like staring at a blank page. This tool makes a clean starter mod folder in one click, so you can begin building your idea right away.


[center]﻿[youtube]7Pnz9T1cfuI[/youtube][/center]


[b][color=#00ff00]What it generates (files + folders)
[/color][/b]
Please note that please do not check generating config file check box in most cases unless you have other specific use, quote from Reddit user shockah:

[quote]The option to create a config file is harmful, [i]please[/i] do not do that, ever. Including a config file with your mod means if someone installs an update for your mod, they lose [i]all of their config[/i].[/quote]

It will create these inside the folder you choose:

[b]Always generated[/b]
[list]
[*][code]manifest.json[/code]
[*][code]i18n/[/code] folder
[list]
[*][code]i18n/default.json[/code]
[/list][/list][b]Optional (if you check the boxes)[/b]
[list]
[*][code]assets/[/code] folder (a place to put images/sounds/data)
[*][code]config.json[/code]
(a starter settings file) (Not recommend to generate in most cases)[*]A basic “code starter set”:
[list]
[*][code]<YourModName>.csproj[/code]
[*][code]ModEntry.cs[/code]
[*][code]ModConfig.cs[/code]
[/list][*][code]IGenericModConfigMenuApi.cs[/code] (a blank helper file for adding a settings menu later)
[/list]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/39913/39913-1766514686-1050820589.png[/img]﻿
[b][color=#00ff00]How to use
[/color][/b]
[list=1]
[*]Open the tool.

[*]Click [b]Browse[/b] and choose (or create) the folder for your new mod.

[*]Choose what you want to generate by checking boxes.

[*]Click [b]Create Files[/b].

[*]Open the new folder and start adding your content when you’re ready.

[/list][b][color=#00ff00]Notes[/color][/b][list]
[*]This tool does [b]not[/b] touch your save or change your game. It only creates a new starter mod folder where you tell it to.
[/list]
[b][color=#ffff00][size=5][center]Instruction to start your own mod[/center][/size][/color][/b]Bascially these steps:    See [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/40579]Daily Pet Bowl Auto-Fill - with instruction on how to make this using AI lol: Mod details[/url]

[b]Run the bot generate all files[/b] --------> [b]filled the file with Codes (have Visual Studio Code free installed)[/b]-------> [b]open [/b][b]csproj file[/b] ---------> [b]Click on Build button on the right panel just right click on some files you will see a build option[/b] ------> [b]any error fix them [/b]------>[b] you will see solution under Bin folder(DLL) pull that out along with manifest and move that to Mod folder (Or if you configre your csproj properly, the built solution will ship the mod straight to your mod folder)[/b]



Want to make a code mod? (Easy setup)You can make mods with/without coding,  checked the [b]“code starter set”[/b] options, the easiest editor is [b]Visual Studio Code[/b] (free).

[list=1]
[*][b]Install Visual Studio Code[/b]

[/list][list]
[*]Download and install [b]Visual Studio Code[/b]
[*]Open it once to finish setup
[/list][list=1]
[*][b]Add C# support (inside Visual Studio Code)[/b]

[/list][list]
[*]Open Visual Studio Code
[*]Click [b]Extensions[/b] (left side icon that looks like 4 squares)
[*]Search [b]“C#”[/b]
[*]Install the [b]official Microsoft C#[/b] extension
[/list][list=1]
[*][b]Install .NET (so your code can run)[/b]

[/list][list]
[*]Install [b].NET 6[/b] (or newer) from Microsoft
[*]Restart your PC if it asks
[/list][list=1]
[*][b]Open your mod folder[/b]

[/list][list]
[*]In Visual Studio Code: [b]File → Open Folder…[/b]
[*]Select the mod folder you created with this tool
[/list][list=1]
[*][b]First test (keep it small)[/b]

[/list][list]
[*]Fill in your mod files with code
[*]Open filled out csproj file, the visual studio code will generate all needed reference dependency for you
[*]click build, if any error, fix them
[*]Save
[*]Launch Stardew Valley and check if your mod loads
[*]If it doesn’t load, you know the drill
[/list]
